record.title: Rabia–al-Yarubiyah inherited interruption and formal reopening, April 2026
record.direction: Not directionally disaggregated; Iraq-to-Syria tanker movement remained prospective
record.movement: Ordinary civilian and commercial access covered by the reopening; first fuel tanker passage unverified
record.exceptions: UN humanitarian consignments and transshipment are documented in 2018–January 2020. Other exceptional traffic is incompletely reconstructed; no all-traffic continuous closure is claimed.
record.imposing_authority: Iraqi and Syrian border/port authorities at restoration; original initiating authority unresolved
record.enforcement: Official restoration is documented; inherited closure is approximate and does not establish an exact continuous operational interval. The separate challenge recovered evidence of a political refusal to regularise access and of humanitarian exceptions.
record.consequences: No general economic effect is quantified by this research packet.
record.relationship: No Rabia–Yaarubiyah parent or phase found in the complete inventory/pending packets. ME006 and ME003 concern Qaim–Al Bukamal; Semalka/Faysh Khabur is a different crossing. No general oil-route announcement is substituted for Rabia operations.
record.status_observation: Historical dated evidence only; an unknown endpoint is not evidence of present open or closed status.
record.current_timing: 2 linked phases; see Chronology phases; do not add overlapping durations
record.current_corrections: Formal permission/restoration at Rabia–al-Yarubiyah is dated 20 April 2026. The inherited interruption is described only approximately and as largely closed; exact onset, continuous exclusion and original imposing order are unknown. Tanker convoys were still prospective in the contemporary Reuters report, so no first actual truck passage or operational duration is assigned. UN humanitarian consignments crossed during March 2018–January 2020, so the inherited restriction cannot mean uninterrupted exclusion of all traffic. The formal restriction on ordinary access is supported by attributed research about blocked reopening; its original order and onset remain unknown.
